correctness.rationale: For each h>=0 the difference-body section equals (1-(1-t)h)B-B by nested Minkowski sums after a translation/shear. Tonelli and mixed-volume multilinearity give the exact volume polynomial. Strict monotonicity is a weighted average of the strictly decreasing ratio Vol(B-s^{-1}B)/Vol(B). Brunn--Minkowski and the published Godbersen theorem give sharp lower/upper bounds and their established equality classifications. Symmetry plus Alexandrov--Fenchel logconcavity make v_j central unimodal; binomial reweighting decreases all increasing functions of distance to the midpoint and gives Var(J)<=m/4. A second-order Taylor bound uniform across all bases yields f(1-u/m)/f(1)=exp(-u/2)+O_T(1/m), followed by the logistic ratio, including tau=0. The exact rational stdlib checker and 20 independently computed 3D convex-hull volumes passed. Finite checks are corroboration, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A natural all-dimensional affine invariant of truncated cones and prisms receives a full, sharp family classification, with both equality families and continuous intermediate values. The main structural insight is a universal dimension-dependent boundary layer for arbitrary sequences of convex bases, independent of smoothness, combinatorial type, or anisotropy; its rate is explicitly O_T(1/m) and uses nontrivial AF coefficient concentration. This is more than a selected numeric invariant or a re-expression of the 2026 Godbersen bound; the exact projection into a one-parameter mixed-volume polynomial and the shape-uniform logistic law are motivated by understanding how a prism loses difference-body symmetry under vanishing homothetic truncation. Residual risk: the elementary section identity might be folklore; the high-dimensional shape-uniform conclusion is the primary substantive contribution.
